sections.html: A slender, very rare Hypostomus imported from Paraguay. The subtropical species tolerates temperatures between 16 and 28°C and attains a maximum length of about 20-25 cm.

South America: Tietê River basin, Ribeira de Iguape River basin, Brazil. Type locality: Rio Tatuhy, left-bank tributary of the Rio Sorocaba, Rio Piracicaba, State of São Paulo [Brazil].

Hypostomus ancistroides is widely distributed, frequent, and abundant. Since no significant threats to its population have been detected, it has been listed in the Least Concern (LC) category (IUCN 2022).

One of the smallest in this genus, it would make a good aquarium inhabitant in a large aquarium. As this genus is in the main messy eaters, good water quality and filtration need to be maintained. A lower water temperature is advised for this species.
Will eat all manner of foods in the aquarium: vegetable foods, tablets, pellets and good quality flake.

Description: Body deep; greatest body depth contained 4.2 to 4.7 and caudal peduncle depth 9.8 to 10.0 times in SL. Mouth inferior. Ground colour brown, with dark-brown blotches on the body, especially on the dorsal region. Fins dark brown with black spots.

Etymology: The specific name ancistroides is Neo-Latin from eidos, form or shape, referring to its resemblance to some species of Ancistrus.
